chunks: From him, from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from al-Sarrad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'I sell weapons.' He said, 'Do not sell them during a fitnah (tribulation/confusion).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling weapons in Shia jurisprudence according to hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) permits the general trade of weapons but advises against selling them during *fitnah*, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on preventing the escalation of civil strife and ensuring arms do not fall into the hands of unjust factions. This ruling underscores the principle of *sadd al-dhara'i* (preventing the means to evil) in commercial jurisprudence, particularly when the political climate is unstable.
